top_story.headline: NASA buys a mission-modified Ford F-59 from Enterprise Rent-A-Car for about $70,000 without competition, citing the Artemis moon schedule
top_story.dek: A company best known for car rentals supplies a specialty truck for the Artemis launch closeout crew, and the agency says there was no time to compete it.
paragraphs: NASA's John F. Kennedy Space Center plans to acquire an existing, mission-modified Ford F-59 from Enterprise Rent-A-Car for an estimated $70,000, with no competition. The justification invokes unusual and compelling urgency. It says the vehicle supports the Exploration Ground Systems Closeout Crew, the team that works with the Artemis launch processing.

According to the justification, the vehicle is already configured and operationally integrated into Artemis launch processing. It says losing it would create operational risk, disrupt mission readiness and potentially affect Artemis launch schedules, and that the timeline does not allow another vehicle to be acquired and modified. It ties the purchase to Executive Order 14369, "Ensuring American Space Superiority," which it describes as directing federal efforts to return American astronauts to the lunar surface no later than 2028.

USAspending shows a federal contract on record under Enterprise Rent-A-Car going back to October 2004, so this is not the company's first government work. The notice carries solicitation number 80KSC026P0014, while the justification text itself refers to 80KSC026P0011.

sections.headline: Immigration agency gives Procentrix a no-bid job to link its alien-file records to the citizenship agency's digital repository
paragraphs: There were 31 new sole-source justifications today, 15 of them posted under other notice types such as Special Notices and Sources Sought. Another 42 repeats from earlier editions were left out. Six that mainly keep an incumbent's contract running are in Extensions, and one is the Top Story.

The day has several urgency-based buys with a story attached: a hospital nurse-call system after two alert failures, a Navy landslide contract signed before its justification was posted, and a post-wildfire mulch purchase.

blocks.text: Must read

blocks.title: Immigration agency adds a no-bid alien-file records job to Procentrix's existing task order
meta: limited-source order (logical follow-on to an existing order)
blocks.text: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement wants to modify its Records and Information Management Unit task order (70CTD024FR0000094, under the SWIFT contract) to add 12 months of Alien-File records modernization, running September 30, 2026 to September 29, 2027. The work would integrate the Office of the Principal Legal Advisor's PLAnet litigation case management system with the U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services STACKS digital A-File repository. The agency says Procentrix LLC must do it because, "As the incumbent, Procentrix has direct, current knowledge" of the system's architecture, and a second vendor would split accountability for records integrity. The justification cites Executive Order 14243 on reducing information silos, and the value is redacted.

blocks.title: Dayton VA hospital buys a nurse-call system upgrade without competition after two alert failures
meta: urgent need, no time to compete
blocks.text: Posted as a Special Notice, this justification covers a Rauland Responder 5 nurse-call upgrade with Vocera integration for Buildings 330 and 320 at the Dayton VA Medical Center, bought through Network Contracting Office 10. The document says the old Responder 4 system is at end of life with no replacement parts. It describes a May 6, 2026 failure of the Vocera interface to route calls to the right staff. On June 3, 2026, at about 2:30 a.m., a veteran fell and disconnected the call-light cord, and "no alarm occurred." Of the authorized Vocera dealers, it says only GMP can supply the Rauland system with the required integration. The value is redacted.

blocks.title: Navy gives Kapule a no-bid landslide cleanup at its Sasebo, Japan base, and signed the contract before posting the justification
meta: urgent need, no time to compete
Department of the Navy (Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command Far East)
blocks.text: A July 6, 2026 rainfall caused a landslide at Commander Fleet Activities Sasebo, and a dislodged boulder remains a hazard. The justification says Public Works first expected Navy Seabees to remove it, but on August 19 it was confirmed they lacked the equipment. A request for proposals went to Kapule, LLC on August 27, and the sole-source contract was awarded September 18, nearly a month before today's posting. The Navy says Kapule was already on the installation for other construction and that competing the work would take two to four months. The contract value is redacted.

blocks.title: Bureau of Land Management buys 6,000 cubic yards of wood mulch from a local logger to protect the Big Rock Fire burn scar
meta: urgent need, no time to compete
Department of the Interior, Bureau of Land Management
blocks.text: Posted as a Special Notice, the justification covers mulch for slopes above Heise, Idaho, where two rain events have already moved material onto roads and private property. It says Wilcox Logging, Inc. is the only source that can deliver in time because the mulch is a byproduct of its logging operation next to the fire area. In market research, one producer said it no longer makes the product, and Mountain Pine Manufacturing quoted $680,000 for the volume.

blocks.title: Marshals Service raises the ceiling on its seized-jewelry auction contract by $4.5 million, to $16.2 million
meta: urgent need, no time to compete
Department of Justice, U.S. Marshals Service
blocks.text: The U.S. Marshals Service Asset Forfeiture Division wants to raise the ceiling on contract 15M50022DA4400016 from $11,738,950 to $16,238,950. The contract was awarded in 2022 as a small-business set-aside and is now in Option Year 4, running to June 30, 2027. The document says more inventory and a surge in precious-metals prices drove costs up, putting the average gold price at $4,000 to $4,100 per ounce today. It also describes the services as handling jewelry, art, antiques and collectibles seized in forfeiture cases.
Also worth a look

The Ginkgo justification says a new contractor would jeopardize demonstrations planned for winter 2026-2027 alongside Arctic exercises. The Michigan record caps all Phase III awards at $5 million, and Ginkgo's value is not verified. (HR001124C0378, HR001124C0315)

Drug Enforcement Administration plans a no-bid site lease from GTP Structures for its Boston antenna site. It was posted as a Special Notice under a class justification for antenna sites for fiscal 2023 through 2028, with no value stated. (D-27-BO-0019)

Defense Logistics Agency buys 37 repair parts for Rough Terrain Container Handlers from Independent Rough Terrain Center without competition. The three-year requirement is value-redacted, and the agency says it owns no technical data on the parts. (SPRDL1-25-R-0153)

Federal Bureau of Prisons pays Johnson Controls $43,000 without competition to repair a failed chiller at Aliceville, Alabama. The document says the prison was running on a single chiller for over 1,000 inmates, including vulnerable medical cases. (15B31827F00000018)

sections.headline: State Department buys $19.6 million of no-bid bridge lodging for foreign service families as its recompete drags on
paragraphs: Six new justifications mainly keep an incumbent's contract running. Two of the bridges involve the Washington area or immigration-adjacent programs, and one supports the Defense Logistics Agency's food supply to ships abroad.

blocks.title: State Department awards no-bid bridge lodging contracts for foreign service personnel after its extension options and contract vehicles ran out
meta: Madison Hospitality Services, LLC; Interim Homes, Inc.; Executive Apartment Inc.
urgent need, no time to compete
blocks.text: The Department of State will replace three expiring task orders with three-month bridge contracts plus a three-month option. They provide furnished housing and shuttles for personnel training at the Shultz Foreign Affairs Training Center in Arlington, Virginia, and for medevac cases in the Washington area. The document says the extension clause was already used in full, the underlying contracts have expired, and the recompete's proposals are still under evaluation. It says families face "the extreme risk of eviction" if the incumbents lapse. It counts 652 families in the program, according to the agency.

blocks.title: Health and Human Services extends Deloitte's repatriation program contract six months without competition
meta: urgent need, no time to compete
Department of Health and Human Services, Administration for Children and Families
blocks.text: Deloitte Consulting LLP held the repatriation evaluation task order for five years (September 30, 2021 to September 29, 2026) with all four option periods exercised. The bridge extends it to March 29, 2027 for operational partner engagements at U.S. ports of entry, a program maturity assessment and finance training. The document says a lapse would hurt readiness for an estimated 600 to 1,000 returning U.S. citizens a year, plus surges during crises. The Administration for Children and Families says transition could not be completed in the time left.

blocks.title: Defense Logistics Agency extends EFS's Europe and North Africa ship food contract for 425 days without competition
meta: only one company can do it
blocks.text: Defense Logistics Agency Troop Support is bridging prime vendor food service for ships in its Europe Zone 4 area through a 425-day fixed-price indefinite-delivery contract. The agency says EFS EBREX Sarl is the only source with a fully implemented catalog and that a new vendor would need a 180-day transition. A separate bridge for Western Africa went to the same company today.

items: Defense Logistics Agency gives EFS another no-bid bridge to supply food to military customers in Western Africa for $700,000. The document file is labeled Western Africa Bridge 2 and cites supply disruptions after the July 2023 Niger military takeover. (SPE30027D4113)

Defense Information Systems Agency plans a no-bid bridge with GCR-DEAN for building operations support at its headquarters. The services include maintenance, custodial, grounds and snow removal, and no value is stated. It was posted as a Special Notice. (612675548)
State Department extends MSI's monitoring, evaluation and analytics services for Middle East and North Africa aid programs without competition. The value is not stated. (19AQMM26F1191)

sections.headline: Court ruling forces the General Services Administration to take new action before awarding its Polaris small business contracts
paragraphs: There were 170 new solicitations, and 204 repeats from earlier editions were left out. Documents read today also turned up several details on notices posted earlier.

blocks.title: General Services Administration says a Court of Federal Claims decision requires action before Polaris small business awards
meta: General Services Administration, Federal Acquisition Service
blocks.text: The General Services Administration says a September 10, 2026 decision in BEAT-LDI JV LLC et al v. The United States (Case No. 25-cv-00082) requires it to act before making awards. Amendment 0013 posted in the Polaris Submission Portal and applies only to offerors that submitted timely proposals by October 7, 2022 and extended their offers through March 31, 2025. All 38 attachments are queued to be read.

blocks.text: The Department of the Air Force wants a five-year blanket purchase agreement for embalming, restoration and disposition of remains. According to the addendum, the preparing mortuary must be "within a 50-mile driving radius of Little Rock AFB, AR." sections.headline: Delayed Pentagon data shows $23.5 million for Booz Allen to support a U.S. Air Force security team at Pakistani air bases
paragraphs: From this morning's edition: USAspending.gov is pulled once a day.

USAspending shows 140 new awards of $2 million or more today, 118 of them Defense Department awards published after the 90-day hold. It also shows 11 large modifications and 11 cuts. The 128 routine ones are listed, each linked, in “USAspending: Every Other New Award” at the end of the edition. One $2 million-plus award worth $2.1 million cites Executive Order 14398. No White House or Executive Office of the President awards turned up.

blocks.text: Most notable

Booz Allen Hamilton Inc. received $23,535,656 from the Department of the Air Force for support services at Pakistan Air Force bases Shahbaz and Mushaf for the U.S. Air Force technical security team and designated representatives. It was signed July 16 and published this week; Defense Department contract data is released with a 90-day delay. (award)

World Wide Technology LLC won $24,446,962 from the Defense Information Systems Agency for a satellite communications kit whose description is tagged “Operation Epic Fury.” It was signed July 16 and published this week. (award)

Northstar Maritime Dismantlement Services, LLC was awarded $415,497,668 by the Department of the Navy to dismantle and dispose of combat ships and landing vessels, signed July 15 and published this week. (award)
StoneX Financial Ltd received two orders from the United States Mint for silver bullion raw material, $32,756,349 and $32,735,314, both dated October 13. (first order, second order)
Terminations

Leidos, Inc.’s contract with the National Institutes of Health was terminated for the convenience of the government on October 13, removing $15,840,826 under FAR 52.249-2. The work was IT business application development support. (award) Booz Allen Hamilton Inc.’s contract with the Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency to operate and enhance the OPIS application suite was also terminated for convenience, removing $6,880,659; signed July 16 and published this week. (award)
